chunks: And from him, from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath, from Ja'far, from his father, upon them be peace, who said:
"Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) disliked that the fasting person should perfume himself with it (musk)."

key_terms.كَرِهَ: Disliked (indicating a recommended dislike or preference in jurisprudence)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on using musk while fasting according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the specific juristic preference (karaha) of Imam Ali (peace be upon him) regarding the use of musk by those fasting. In Shia fiqh, this distinction is significant because it differentiates between scents that are absorbed through the nose (like musk) and those that are merely perceived, influencing the validity of the fast according to various scholars. It reflects the meticulous attention to sensory details in the purification of worship during Ramadan.
